rules.title: OT and IT workloads do not share a hypervisor host
rules.rationale: A host that runs both IT and plant workloads makes the hypervisor a bridge between zones: compromising the host through any IT guest, or escaping one IT guest, reaches the OT systems on the same host.

mitigation.summary: Run OT workloads on dedicated hosts or a dedicated cluster.
steps: Create an OT host group or cluster
Migrate OT VMs and add VM-host affinity rules
Keep IT VMs off those hosts

rules.limitations: Virtualization layer only. OT and IT are taken from scope zones with purdueLevel; workload VMs with no level count as IT.

rules.title: OT and IT workloads do not share a virtual switch
rules.rationale: OT and IT VMs on one virtual switch or libvirt network share a layer-2 domain and switch configuration, so one misconfigured portgroup, VLAN or promiscuous setting bridges the zones. Portgroups of one distributed switch count as that switch.

mitigation.summary: Attach OT workloads to a dedicated virtual switch with dedicated uplinks.
steps: Create an OT virtual switch (or libvirt network) with its own uplinks
Move OT VM adapters to it
Route IT-to-OT traffic only through the OT DMZ firewall

rules.limitations: Virtualization layer only; physical switching and VLAN trunking beyond the host are not assessed.

rules.title: OT hosts have their own management plane
rules.rationale: A management plane that manages hosts running OT and IT workloads lets any compromise of it, or of its IT-side administrators, reach the plant. IEC 62443 expects OT management to sit in its own zone or behind a conduit.

mitigation.summary: Manage OT hosts from a dedicated vCenter or cluster in the OT zone.
steps: Deploy a management instance for OT hosts in the OT zone
Allow access from IT only through the OT DMZ jump host

rules.title: No identity administers both OT and IT hosts
rules.rationale: A principal with admin rights on a host running OT workloads and on an IT host (directly, through a group or through a vCenter that manages both) is an identity bridge: stealing that one credential on the IT side hands over the plant hypervisors.

mitigation.summary: Use separate OT administrator accounts and groups with no IT rights.
steps: Grant them rights on OT hosts or the OT management plane only
Remove IT admin groups from OT hosts

rules.limitations: Derived from collected vCenter permissions, Hyper-V local groups and KVM admin groups; AD group nesting is followed only when declared in identityGroups.

rules.title: No IT entry point reaches an OT workload
rules.rationale: The blast-radius graph links network policy, management reachability and admin rights. A path from an IT workload to an OT workload means one IT compromise can reach the plant through the virtualization layer.

mitigation.summary: Break the path at the cheapest hop shown in the Blast radius view.
steps: Open the path in the Blast radius view
Remove the admin right, network rule or management exposure it uses
Re-run VSAT to confirm the path is gone

rules.limitations: Configuration-inferred reachability within the bounded blast-radius search; entry points are representative IT workloads unless declared in entryPoints.

rules.title: IT workloads reach plant workloads only through the OT DMZ
rules.rationale: Purdue level 0-2 systems should accept traffic from IT only through the level 3.5 OT DMZ. A direct network allow from an IT workload to a plant workload bypasses the DMZ and its inspection.

mitigation.summary: Deny direct IT-to-plant traffic and route it through the OT DMZ.
steps: Add a firewall rule denying IT sources to level 0-2 groups
Publish required data through DMZ brokers or historians

rules.limitations: Configuration-inferred from distributed firewall policy and shared virtual switches, evaluated for the IT entry workloads of the blast-radius search.
